quotes.text: "test increment concurrency" needs to be more precise so future readers of this code understand the guarantee we're making. This is testing the _I_ in ACID, that `#increment!` isn't vulnerable to stale reads.

quotes.text: @jeremy Maybe the changes fix some bugs when counter cache is only updated in DB but not on instance, but it is hard to assume where it happens and if it really happens. We have no identity map and we can not be sure we updated all instances in memory with a proper counter value.

quotes.text:
So this patch includes the following changes:
- Reuse code between increment and decrement methods
- Extracted a code snippet (search for ultimate 'eww' comment in diff)
  from has_many association internals to #increment! method
- Make use of `#increment!` and `#decrement!` methods where possible
  instead of `.update_counters` that doesn't update an counters on
  record instance level
quotes.author: bogdan
quotes.title: Make AR#increment! AR#decrement! concurency safe

medium: These passages reveal concerns about concurrency safety, potential data inconsistencies with counter caching, and the need for precise testing.

case.deletion_subject: Remove `counter_cache_target` which is no longer called

revert_subject: Revert "Remove `counter_cache_target` which is no longer called"
answer: When inverse_of is disabled, counters are incremented without an inflated parent target; without this check it runs extra queries to load the parent.
